description.narrative: Overall Programme Objective: To support the sustainable transition of partner local selfgovernment units (LSGUs) in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This will be achieved through: 1) Improved Environmental Governance: By enhancing capacities and resources in BiH for efficient and effective implementation of the environmental strategy and by 2) Effective Local Transition Measures: By creating and implementing effective local transition measures and policies, thus contributing to better living conditions for citizens in coal regions in BiH. Two Intermediate Outcomes: Improved environmental sustainability and resilience of partner LSGUs in BiH Implementation of systemic transition measures aligned with the Green Agenda, driving inclusive and sustainable local development Three Immediate Outcomes: Improved policy framework and financing for sustainable transition Enhanced skills and knowledge of local stakeholders utilizing Swedish expertise Raised awareness and acceptance for sustainability and just transition

Programme “Sustainable Transition of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH SuTra)” aims to improve country-wide approach and national and local capacities to implement efficiently and effectively environmental and sustainable transition policies in BiH. The Programme consists of 2 Components, Component 1 – Environmental Governance & Capacity Building, with a duration of 60 months, and Component 2 – Supporting the Transition of Coal Regions in BiH, with a duration of 36 months, which will be implemented in parallel with Component 1 from the beginning. The Programme builds on the momentum created by the predecessor project that the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) implemented with the financial support of Sida – “Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Environmental Strategy (BIH ESAP 2030+)”,. The programme considers the lessons learned from BIH ESAP 2030+ and its established processes, structure, and extensive stakeholder network.

Programmet "Hållbar omställning i Bosnien och Hercegovina (BiH SuTra)" syftar till att förbättra den landsomfattande strategin och den nationella och lokala kapaciteten för att effektivt och ändamålsenligt genomföra politik för miljön och den hållbara omställningen i Bosnien och Hercegovina. Programmet består av två komponenter, komponent 1 - Miljöförvaltning och kapacitetsuppbyggnad, med en varaktighet på 60 månader, och komponent 2 - Stöd till Bosnien och Hercegovinas kolregioners omställning, med en varaktighet på 36 månader. Komponent 2 kommer från start att genomföras parallellt med komponent 1. Programmet bygger vidare på det som skapades av det föregångsprojekt som Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI) genomförde med finansiellt stöd från Sida - "Bosniens och Hercegovinas miljöstrategi (BIH ESAP 2030+)". Programmet tar hänsyn till lärdomarna från BIH ESAP 2030+ och det projektets etablerade processer, struktur och omfattande nätverk av intressenter.

Due to continuous absence of progress in the adoption process of the Environmental Strategy BIH (BIH ESAP), in March 2025 Sweden has decided to cancel its funding for project component 1 (PC1), aimed at support to BIH, entity, and Brcko District level institutions in implementation of measures from the strategy. Consequently the project has been amended in April 2025 reallocating funds from PC1 to PC2 and expanding a number of municipalities being supported by SEIs technical assistance in developing and implementing their transitional plans, amongst the others.
Following this, in 2025, SEI expanded its partnership base and is now actively working with seven local self-government units (LSGUs), 4 supported from beginning of the project and 3 included after an amendment. Following bit delayed adoption of the Operational Plan for Banovii SEI initiated the participatory preparation of Transitional Plans for three new municipalities. Across four municipalities, six short-term priority activities were implemented or advanced, resulting in the preparation and/or formal adoption of key technical documents, the establishment of new digital management tools, and amendments to Operational Plans. Five trainings and a study tour increased capacity of more than 120 participants. As an outcome, these activities directly strengthened the capacities of nearly 200 municipal staff, enabling more effective planning, management, and decision-making. Through project and additional impact initiatives, SEI engaged almost 1,500 people via meetings, workshops, and other forms of engagement.
Overall, the project has made a good progress, delivering a range of activities and outputs aligned with its ambitious objectives. More specifically, the following key results were achieved during reporting period:
In 2025, the BiH SuTra partnership was expanded to ensure Bosnia and Herzegovinas territorial and thematic transition needs are fully reflected. Building on the 2023's criteria for selection of partner municipalities (municipalities from coal reagions, with expresed interest and proved commitment for reforms, even geographical coverage, etc..), SEI and state and entity ministries agreed to add new LSGUs to close geographic gaps, include remaining coalrelated municipalities, and pilot Transition Plans in strong noncoal communities. This expansion identified Kakanj, Gacko, and Gradika as the most suitable new partners, all of which demonstrated clear interest, readiness, and capacities. Each municipality submitted the required documentation and appointed focal points, enabling project activities to begin in September 2025, when SEI signed the Memorandum of Understanding with new LSGUs, and revised MoUs with old LSGUs.
Work Package 1 Defining Sustainable Transition Pathways
The baseline assessment (including the introduction, methodology, development pathways chapters) within the Transitional Plan (TP) has been developed in the period September December 2025 for the three new partner LSGUs. These include a collection and analysis of officially available data for each LSGU, analysed for each sector within each of the five development pathways.
A series of participatory Vision 2050 workshops were held in Gacko, Kakanj and Gradika during October 2025. In total, around 120 participants took part in the on-site events (59 women, 62 men), representing local governments, public utilities, businesses, civil society, academia and citizens. Using a facilitated and highly participatory methodology, stakeholders co-created local 2050 visions aligned with the five pillars of the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans. Each LSGU reflected its specific context, coal transition in Gacko and Kakanj, and green growth and smart development in Gradika, all visions emphasized economic diversification, environmental restoration, improved infrastructure, and social cohesion as cornerstones of a sustainable future.
The development of Transitional Plans for new partners has started in September 2025, with the development of baseline assessment, collection of available data and mapping of stakeholders for each LSGU. Local experts will be engaged in early 2026, while SEIs goal is to develop three Transitional Plans by Summer 2026 and have them ready for adoption at municipal councils/city council at the end of August 2026.
SEI is also supporting the four LSGUs, which have entered the partnership with the BiH SuTra project in 2023, with the update of their short-term measures/activities in the Operational Plans. In December 2025, the City of Zivinice and the Municipality of Ugljevik, supported by SEI, updated their Operational Plans as a logical continuation of their work on towards the fulfilment of the Green Agenda targets and the results and findings of the conducted technical assistance for the development and adoption of short-term transition priorities.
Work Package 2. Enabling Transitional Processes
SEI continued with Technical Assistance for the development and adoption of short-term transition priorities in 4 LSGUs from first phase.
In 2025, partner local self-government units operationalized their Transition Plans (20252027) through concrete, council-adopted measures. The four municipalities implemented /advanced six short-term priority activities, resulting in the preparation and/or formal adoption of key technical documents, development of local capacities, and amendments to Operational Plans. These results demonstrate strengthened municipal capacity for evidence-based planning, improved environmental governance, and increased readiness for future green investments aligned with EU and Green Agenda priorities.
ivinice completed and formally adopted two priority outputs. First, a GIS (Geo Information System)-based digital public lighting register covering the entire city's territory was established, alongside a comprehensive energy audit of the public lighting system. Second, a Sustainable Urban Transport Study was prepared and adopted by the City Council
Ugljevik advanced implementation of one strategic priority activity, the development of the Wastewater Management System until 2050, including preparation of conceptual design and initial technical-investment documentation. In addition, the Municipal Council formally amended the Operational Plan to include development of the main design for a wastewater pumping station, accelerating implementation readiness.
Breza progressed with preparation of conceptual and initial technical documentation for its long-term Wastewater Management System (until 2050). Although completion was extended due to technical adjustments regarding plant location, the process strengthened strategic planning capacity and clarified future investment steps.
Banovii initiated implementation of two priority activities. The first established the foundation for a monitoring and enforcement system addressing illegal waste disposal, including installation planning for surveillance equipment, development of digital reporting tools, and staff capacity-building measures. The second launched an agri-food promotion and rural development initiative, including development of a branding and promotion framework for local products, support for small enterprises, and institutional cooperation mechanisms.
All activities described are implemented under continuous quality assurance and expert supervision provided by SEI and Swedish niche experts. This ensures alignment with international standards and best practices, methodological rigor, and consistency with the strategic objectives of the Transition Plan 2050 (Green Agenda).
Following the planned finalization of short-term measures in the four LSGUs in late 2025 and early 2026 (ivinice, Ugljevik and Breza), technical assistance for the development of project fiches will take place in 2026. The most promising candidates are Ugljevik and Breza for their waste-water treatment facilities, as well as ivinice for their sustainable transportation follow up. Banovii will finalize their first short-term measures/priorities in mid-2026.
LSGUs expressed genuine concern regarding unclear land ownership, power imbalances, and limited authority over postmining land use, despite municipalities bearing the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of coal mining. This shared challenge was raised by multiple municipalities during discussions in 2025, leading to consultations with entitylevel ministries in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which acknowledged the issue and agreed on the need for a structured, multilevel dialogue. As a result, a closed roundtable planned for May/June 2026 will bring together local governments, ministries, utilities, and mining companies to identify barriers and establish guidelines for better coordination on postmining land management.
Work Package 3 Support to Learning and Knowledge Exchange
On the job training and Technical Assistance for Public Utility JP Eko Sep d.o.o. in Zivinice has started in September 2025. The support aims to strengthen the operators capacity for evidence-based decision-making and improved planning of landfill operations, including considerations for circular economy approaches and collecting the data to support planning for potential Phase II investment options.
During 2025, the project successfully conducted three capacity-building trainings steaming from the CB Needs Assessment, engaging approximately 80 participants and strengthening the skills and knowledge of local government staff across partner municipalities:
Training on Sustainable Agriculture was held in June 2025 in Ugljevik as a hybrid training, focusing on strengthening LSGU capacities in climate-smart and sustainable farming.
Training on District Heating held in Banovici, Bosnia and Herzegovina in November 2025, bringing together 31 participants from partner LSGUs, public utilities, private consultancies, coal companies, and international organizations.
Wastewater management (December 2025) was held in Breza, Bosnia and Herzegovina, with 28 participants from local administrations, utilities, water-sector institutions, and project experts.
Study visit to Sweden has been organized in May 2025, aimed to support peer learning and cooperation between partner LSGUs and Swedish counterparts, but also as a part of the Capacity Building Needs Assessment carried out in December 2024.
In 2025, preparatory work began for peer-to-peer learning and long-term cooperation between Bosnian and Swedish municipalities, providing a structured basis for launching activities, engaging municipalities, and formalizing at least one cooperation partnership during the activities of the SuTra project in 2026 and/or early 2027
Gender Equality, Social Equity and Poverty (gesep)
SEI actively integrated GESEP (Gender and Social Equity Perspective) into the organization of stakeholder workshops by providing clear guidelines on accommodating the needs of diverse groups. This included ensuring that all representatives could participate effectively, and that workshop materials were accessible, readable, and understandable to all. As a result, women accounted for over 40% of consultation participants, including representatives from civil society organizations and advocates for disability rights.
In addition, SEI has reviewed and proved feedback on Transitional Plans, ensuring that GESEP-responsive activities and key socio-economic considerations, including public participation, were incorporated.
Stakeholder Engagement and Synergies with Other Projects
SEI maintains regular meetings with the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations, line energy ministries, cantonal institutions, and other projects and institutions, ensuring continuous communication and coordination. As the main beneficiary of the project, MoFTER plays key role aligning different actors, events, and processes, maintaining continuous engagement with LSGUs, and involving key regional stakeholders, including civil society organizations.
Communication with entity ministries improved during 2024 and 2025, especially with Repbulika Srspka that was not responsive in 2023. Both the Federal and Republika Srpska ministries responsible for energy Annual Report 2025 were informed about the project and its expansion, raised no objections, and expressed satisfaction with the project and the cooperation. Moreover, a stable working relationship has been established in relation to multi-level governance activities, with both ministries being active and responsive. In this regard, efforrts will continue with the aim to achieve an increased ownership in relation to this.
SEI also maintains a list of relevant projects and institutions both for internal awareness and knowledge sharing, engaging with these stakeholders regularly, meeting them as needed to exchange information, explore synergies, and coordinate activities.
Transfer of Swedish Know-How
In 2025, SEI has supported BiH by transferring Swedish expertise, promoting climate-resilient planning, circular economy practices, and sustainable urban development, through capacity-building, study tours and direct technical support. This has been achieved through the engagement of SEI and other Swedish experts knowledgeable in key topics. As part of BiH SuTra, ivinice and neighboring municipalities are improving waste management through the EkoSep regional landfill and recycling center, supported by the EU, Sweden (Sida), and EBRD, advancing EU environmental standards and enabling circular economy practices in the region. Moreover, SEI has identified opportunities to align activities with existing SEI projects connected to the Net Zero Cities and Viable Cities as a strategic Swedish program. Within this framework, SEI has developed a Climate Investment Planning tool that can be tailored to the needs of BiH, complementing transitional plans.
SEI is also contributing Swedish perspectives to other projects implemented in BiH. In September 2025, SEI hosted a lecture for participants from BiH as part of a study tour organized by the Folke Bernadotte Academy, presenting work on climate risks, hazard management, and climate adaptation in Sweden, as well as insights from the BiH SuTra.
SEI has also taken a proactive approach by engaging with other Swedish actors, such as the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, Business Sweden and Confederation of Swedish Enterprises.
